## Memory copilot

With the `memory` tag, the long-term memory copilot runs its own small model loop before and after a turn and calls these tools itself; they are not in the registry and the main model never sees them (`external/memory/copilot.go`, `external/memory/tools`). The recall phase gets the first three, the persist phase all six. Paths are `scope:relative/path.md` ([Long-term memory](../features/memory.md#the-tools)).

| Tool | Purpose | Arguments (short) | Permission | Modes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `coddy_memory_search` | Rank the notes under the chosen roots against a query | `query`, `scope` | none | copilot only |
| `coddy_memory_list` | List directories and notes one level under a path | `path` | none | copilot only |
| `coddy_memory_read` | Read one note | `path` | none | copilot only |
| `coddy_memory_mkdir` | Create nested folders under a scope | `path` | none | copilot only |
| `coddy_memory_save` | Write or overwrite a note | `title`, `body`, `scope`, `relative_path` | none | copilot only |
| `coddy_memory_delete` | Delete a note or a folder with everything under it, never a root | `path` | none | copilot only |

## MCP tools

Every enabled tool of every connected MCP server joins the same function-calling list under the name `server__tool`, with the server's own input schema and a description prefixed with `[server]` (`internal/mcp/client.go`; [MCP servers](../features/mcp.md#tool-namespacing)). Because `__` is the separator, a server name may not contain it. The definitions are appended in agent and plan mode and never in ask mode, where a call to such a name is refused at execution time. A call whose name contains `__` bypasses the registry: the agent routes it to the owning server and applies the `default` output limit to the result. There is no built-in permission prompt for MCP calls; whether a server may start is the workspace trust decision, and the per-server and per-tool disable switches bound what a running server may do ([MCP servers](../features/mcp.md#permission-model)).

## What runs before a tool call

Operator hooks see every call, MCP tools included, before the permission gate and whatever the permission mode ([Hooks](../features/hooks.md#what-a-hook-answers)). A `PreToolUse` hook answering `permissionDecision: deny` stops the call; it is never executed and the model reads `blocked by hook: <reason>` as the tool result. `allow` skips the prompt a tool would otherwise raise, `ask` forces one even under `accept_edits` or `bypass`, and `updatedInput` replaces the argument object before the call runs. Several matching hooks all run, and the most restrictive decision wins.

A subagent's tool set is narrowed from the parent's ([Subagents](../features/subagents.md#how-capabilities-narrow)): a definition's `tools` and `disallowed_tools` only remove names, and `question`, the five config editing tools and `plan_exit` are excluded from every child, so a child can neither ask the user nor rewrite the configuration nor leave plan mode. Results are capped by `tools.output_limits` before they reach the model, for built-in and MCP tools alike.


# Reference / HTTP API

Source: https://coddy.dev/docs/reference/http-api.md

# OpenAI-compatible HTTP API

The HTTP surface ships only when the binary is built with **`go build -tags=http`** (`make build TAGS=http`). It exposes OpenAI-shaped routes plus **`/coddy/*`** helpers, backed by the same session manager and ReAct agent as **`coddy acp`**.

It is not a command of its own. **`coddy serve`** runs it whenever **`httpserver.enable`** is true, which it is unless the file says otherwise, alongside every other subsystem the configuration enables - the Telegram gateway, the swarm relay, the cron scheduler. They share one session manager, so a conversation a bot started is a session this API lists, streams and can continue.

The bundled SPA is included only when you also set the **`ui`** tag (for example **`make build TAGS="http ui"`** or **`go build -tags=http,ui`**). With **http** only, **`GET /`** returns **404** with a plain-text hint.

## OpenAPI and Swagger UI

Specs are regenerated on each request so they stay aligned with handlers.

- **`GET /openapi.yaml`** - OpenAPI 3.0 (YAML); **`GET /openapi.json`** mirrors it in JSON (both **`Content-Disposition: inline`**).
- **`GET /docs/`** - Swagger UI (static assets bundled in the binary, no CDN). **`GET /docs`** redirects to **`/docs/`**.

## Authentication (optional)

Authentication is **off by default** (historical behavior). Set a bearer token to protect the
API when exposing it beyond loopback:

- `httpserver.auth_token` in `config.yaml` (supports `${ENV}`), or
- `--auth-token <token>` on `coddy serve`, or
- the `CODDY_HTTP_TOKEN` environment variable.

When a token is configured, every `/v1/*` and `/coddy/*` route requires
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` and returns `401` with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` challenge
otherwise. The SPA shell and static assets stay public so a client can load and prompt for the
token; `/docs` and `/openapi.*` are protected unless `httpserver.public_docs: true`. The token is
never returned by `GET /coddy/config` (redacted; the DTO only reports `auth_configured`). Tokens
passed via `--auth-token` / `CODDY_HTTP_TOKEN` are never written to `config.yaml` and survive
`PUT /coddy/config` hot reloads. Prefer TLS (or a TLS-terminating proxy) when using auth over a
network. Binding a non-loopback address without a token logs a startup warning unless
`httpserver.allow_insecure: true`.

Without a token the surface is unauthenticated; run behind appropriate network controls.

### Cross-origin access and the remote UI

The bundled UI can point at a **remote** `coddy serve` server (an environment selector switches
the API base URL and sends the remote's bearer token). Because that is a cross-origin call, the
remote server must opt into CORS:

```yaml
httpserver:
  auth_token: "${CODDY_HTTP_TOKEN}"
  cors:
    enable: true
    allowed_origins: ["http://localhost:12345", "https://my-ui.example"]   # or ["*"]
  remotes:                       # optional: offered in the UI environment selector
    - name: "prod box"
      url: "https://box.example:12345"
```

When `cors.enable` is true, preflight `OPTIONS` requests for an allowed origin return `204` with
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (echoed origin, or `*` when configured) and
`Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type, X-Coddy-Session-ID`; disallowed origins
receive no CORS headers. Bearer auth still applies to the actual request. Tokens for remotes are
**not** stored in `httpserver.remotes`; the UI keeps them client-side per remote.

Because `EventSource` cannot send an `Authorization` header cross-origin, the two SSE
subscription routes - **`GET /coddy/sessions/{id}/composer-stream`** and **`GET /coddy/events`**
- also accept the token as a `?access_token=` query parameter. No other route does; prefer the
header where the client can set one, since a query token reaches proxy access logs.

## Embedded web UI (**`-tags=http,ui`**)

- **`GET /`** serves **`index.html`**, **`styles.css`**, and **`app.js`** from **`external/ui/`** (`go:embed`) when **`ui`** is set at link time with **`http`**. Responses for **`/`**, **`/index.html`**, **`/app.js`**, and **`/styles.css`** include **`Cache-Control: no-cache`** so a normal reload picks up assets after you rebuild the binary (fixed URLs, no fingerprint).
- **API-only mode**: set **`ui.enable: false`** in config to run the server without the SPA even when the **`ui`** tag is compiled in. **`GET /`** then returns a short plaintext notice (HTTP 404) instead of the UI; every **`/v1/*`** and **`/coddy/*`** route keeps working and keeps requiring **`httpserver.auth_token`** when set. Useful for a headless remote box other UIs connect to.
- Recommended session URL pattern: **`#/s/<sessionId>`** (client-only history). For **`POST /v1/responses`** and **`POST /v1/chat/completions`**, send **`X-Coddy-Session-ID`** with a **`sess_<hex>`** id that satisfies server-side validation (`internal/session/validate.go`).
- **`GET /coddy/sessions`**, **`PATCH /coddy/sessions/{id}`**, and other **`/coddy/sessions/{id}/...`** routes identify the session **only** by the **`{id}`** path segment (no duplicate header in OpenAPI; clients may still send **`X-Coddy-Session-ID`**, it is not used to pick the resource for those URLs).
- The bundled UI calls **`POST /v1/responses`** with **`stream: true`**. If **`GET /coddy/sessions`** reports **`turnActive`** for the open session (for example after a full tab reload while another client or the same server process still runs the turn), the UI subscribes to **`GET /coddy/sessions/{id}/composer-stream`** (SSE) to replay bytes already emitted for that turn and continue receiving live chunks until **`data: [DONE]`** or an error event. Starting a new **`POST /v1/responses`** cancels that relay subscription client-side. For ReAct (**`model`** **`agent`**, **`plan`**, or **`ask`**), it sends optional **`metadata.model`** with the selected YAML **`models[].model`** **`id`** and optional **`metadata.runPlanSlug`** to implement a saved design plan (**`coddy.dev/runPlanSlug`** on ACP **`session/prompt`**; answered with **`409`** before the turn starts when **`model`** is **`ask`**) (from **`GET /v1/models`**, **`owned_by`** not **`coddy`**); default follows **`default_agent_model`**, persisted choice in **`coddy_llm_model`**. When the selected model exposes **`reasoning_levels`**, it also sends optional **`metadata.reasoning`** with the chosen level; default follows the model's **`reasoning_default`**, persisted choice in **`coddy_llm_reasoning`**. It derives **`attachments`** from **`@path`** mentions in **`input`** (files only); a mention may narrow a file to a line range (**`@Dockerfile:21-31`**), which travels as **`attachments[].source.startLine`** / **`endLine`** and reaches the model as **`<coddy_attachment ... lines="21-31">`** holding only those lines. **`GET /coddy/workspace/files`** powers the **`@`** picker and **`GET /coddy/workspace/file`** powers the line-range picker that opens after the **`:`**. SSE **default** chunks follow **`chat.completion.chunk`** deltas (**`delta.content`** for assistant text, **`delta.reasoning_content`** for streamed model reasoning so the UI can keep the **thinking** foldout separate). Named **`event:`** lines (**`tool_call`**, **`tool_call_update`**, **`plan`**, **`token_usage`**, **`available_commands`**) expose tool progress and incremental token totals between LLM rounds; the turn stream reserves **`provider_usage`** for a snapshot emitted mid-turn (nothing emits one today; the account usage of a finished turn is read from **`GET /coddy/providers/{name}/usage`** or arrives on **`GET /coddy/events`**); when **`memory.enable`** is **true**, the server also emits **`memory_phase`** (**`sessionUpdate`** **`memory_phase`**) and **`memory_chunk`** (**`memory_message_chunk`**) for the unified memory copilot (**one pass before the main model**, recall-or-persist), streamed model text deltas only, without adding rows to **`messages.json`**. **`GET /coddy/sessions/{id}/messages`** may include **`memoryTurns`** (array of persisted per-turn summaries for the bundled UI transcript). **`coddy_meta`** JSON follows the usual rule immediately before **`data: [DONE]`**; for agent/plan/ask turns it also carries **`stop_reason`** (`end_turn`, `cancelled`, `max_turns`, ...) so remote clients recover the ACP stop reason. **Stop generation** in the composer calls **`POST /coddy/sessions/{id}/cancel`** with **`X-Coddy-Session-ID`** matching **`{id}`**, then **`AbortSignal`** tears down the streamed **`fetch`**. That maps to ACP **`session/cancel`** for the agent turn (**`TurnCtx`** propagation for direct **`models[].model`** completions uses the same cancel hook). Cancel mid-stream still **persists** accumulated assistant **`content`** for that turn; **`GET /coddy/sessions/{id}/messages`** can briefly trail that write, so the SPA **merges** fetched rows with its per-session shadow or on-screen transcript (**`mergeTranscriptPreferLocalSuffix`** in **`external/ui/src/ui/chat/transcriptServerSnapshot.ts`**). More than one session may stream in parallel (**`pickStreamMutationBase`** in **`streamMutationBase.ts`** keeps SSE mutations scoped per **`X-Coddy-Session-ID`**).
- On the first user message of a brand-new chat (no session in the rail yet), the UI **`POST`**s **`/coddy/describe`** in parallel with **`/v1/responses`**. When **`short`** arrives, the header and session list titles update **immediately**; **`PATCH /coddy/sessions/{id}`** still runs once headers expose the canonical session id (**retries PATCH** briefly if persistence lags describe).
- The bundled UI exposes **Settings** at **`#/settings`**. It loads **`GET /coddy/config/schema`** (JSON Schema for the editor) and **`GET /coddy/config`** (current values, including **API keys**, optional per-provider **`proxy`** URLs, and the **`gateways.telegram.token`** bot token), then **`POST /coddy/config/validate`** and **`PUT /coddy/config`** on save. The logical-model form additionally calls **`GET /coddy/providers/{name}/models`** behind **Fetch models** and **`GET /coddy/config/reasoning-levels`** behind **Fetch reasoning levels**, which fills **`models[].reasoning_levels`** with the tiers detected for the model id being edited (the type of the provider row it points at is sent as **`provider_type`**, so an unsaved provider is honoured). The **`gateways`** block round-trips through this API, so editing settings in the UI no longer drops the Telegram configuration. There is no separate auth on these routes - expose **`coddy serve`** only on trusted networks.

- **Current context usage** is a separate named SSE event, **`usage_update`**, with **`used`** and **`size`**. It is re-emitted after manual or automatic compaction. **`token_usage`** remains the completed model-call counter and is not used as the context-window numerator.

## Endpoint summary

| Method | Path | Notes |
|--------|------|-------|
| GET | `/` | Embedded web UI (**`-tags=http,ui`**) or **404** with a hint (**`http` only**). **`Cache-Control: no-cache`** on **`/`**, **`/index.html`**, **`/app.js`**, **`/styles.css`** when the UI module is linked. |
| GET | `/openapi.yaml`, `/openapi.json` | Spec. |
| GET | `/docs`, `/docs/` | Swagger UI. |
| GET | `/v1/models` | Merged list: **`agent`**, **`plan`**, **`ask`** (each **`owned_by`**: **`coddy`**), then every YAML **`models[].model`** row (**`id`** is the selector; **`owned_by`** is the provider prefix). Ordering is **`agent`**, **`plan`**, **`ask`**, then **`models`** in configuration order (same ordering the server emits). Use any returned **`id`** as **`model`** on POST. The JSON object also includes optional **`default_agent_model`**, the configured **`agent.model`** (**`models[].model`**), when set; the bundled UI uses it as the default **`metadata.model`** for ReAct (**`agent`** / **`plan`** / **`ask`**) requests. Each **`models[].model`** row also carries **`max_context_tokens`** (UI hint; 0 or absent for coddy-session profiles) and **`multimodal`** (**`true`** when **`models[].multimodal: true`** in YAML; the bundled UI shows a file attachment button in the composer when the selected model has **`multimodal: true`**). Reasoning models also carry **`reasoning_levels`** (array, e.g. **`["minimal","low","medium","high"]`**; absent for non-reasoning models) and optional **`reasoning_default`** (level pre-selected for new chats); the bundled UI shows a reasoning-level selector in the composer when **`reasoning_levels`** is non-empty. Models served by a **`type: codex`** provider report **`none`** where the model id alone would imply **`minimal`**, because the Codex backend rejects that tier. |
| POST | `/v1/chat/completions` | **`stream`**, **`messages`** (last **`user`**). **`409`** when another **agent**, **plan**, or **ask** turn already holds the session turn lock (exclusive per persisted bundle), and **`409`** when **`X-Coddy-Session-ID`** names a child session spawned by **`spawn_agent`** (**`sub_`** ids): those transcripts are read-only for every model kind, and the error names the parent session to prompt instead. |
| POST | **`/v1/responses`** | **`model`**, **`input`**, optional **`stream`**, optional **`attachments`** ( **`path`** workspace-relative under session cwd, **`agent`** / **`plan`** / **`ask`** only; file bodies are hydrated as text - a file stored in another detected encoding, such as Windows-1251, is converted to UTF-8; server rejects traversal, oversized, non-text (binary or undetectable encoding), and folder **`path`**; optional **`source.startLine`** / **`source.endLine`** narrow a file to a 1-based inclusive line range that the model sees as **`lines="N-M"`**, and a range the file cannot honour is a **`400`**), optional **`inline_files`** (array of **`{name, data_url}`**; **`data_url`** is a `data:<mime>;base64,...` URI; works for all modes — direct YAML model and **`agent`** / **`plan`** / **`ask`**). For **`agent`** / **`plan`** / **`ask`**: each file is saved to the session **`assets/`** directory (`~/.coddy/sessions/<id>/assets/`) with **`0o444`** (read-only) permissions; the model receives a `<coddy_session_assets>` annotation in the user message so it can `read` or `cp` the files without re-transmitting their bytes over the API. For direct YAML model: each entry becomes an image content part on the user message so multimodal models receive the file inline. **`input`** remains the full composer text including **`@path`** echoes. Keeps history between turns when using headers. **`409`** when another **agent**, **plan**, or **ask** turn already holds the session turn lock, for streaming and non-streaming calls alike, and **`409`** when **`X-Coddy-Session-ID`** names a child session spawned by **`spawn_agent`** (**`sub_`** ids): those transcripts are read-only for every model kind, and the error names the parent session to prompt instead. Every **agent** / **plan** / **ask** turn is published to the session's composer relay whatever **`stream`** is set to, so other clients can watch it over **`GET /coddy/sessions/{id}/composer-stream`**; with **`stream: false`** the response body is unchanged. A **`stream: false`** turn is cancelled when its HTTP request is dropped, a streamed one keeps running. A streamed response that has produced no frame for 15s sends an SSE comment keepalive, so a turn on a YAML model with **`stream: false`** - silent on the wire until the whole answer is generated - is not dropped by an idle-timeout proxy. Note the two unrelated meanings of **`stream`**: this request field selects the response shape for the client, while **`models[].stream`** in **config.yaml** selects the transport coddy uses to reach the LLM. |
| GET | `/v1/responses/{id}` | Session metadata snapshot. |
| GET | **`/coddy/sessions`** | Pagination via **`limit`/`cursor`** (cursor is numeric offset token). Optional **`q`** substring filter (**case-insensitive**) over **`session.json` title OR the **first persisted `user`** message **`content`** in `messages.json` order (`system`, `assistant`, `tool`, etc. before that first `user` are ignored). **`q` is not full-text search** over the transcript. Pagination applies **after** filtering. Rows sort by **`session.json` `updatedAt`** (newest first), then **`id`** for stable ties; **`updatedAt`** moves forward on persistence (new turns, title pin, etc.), not when the server only loads a bundle to serve **GET** requests. **`include_scheduler=true`** includes session bundles created for **scheduler runs** (they set **`schedulerRun`** in **`session.json`** and are **omitted** from the default composer list). **`include_subagents=true`** includes child sessions spawned by **`spawn_agent`** (**`sub_`** ids with **`subagentRun`** in **`session.json`**, hidden by default); each such row carries **`subagent`** **`{parentSessionId, name, taskId}`** read from its bundle, and the default listing opens no child bundle. **`include_activity=true`** adds **`turnActive`**, **`activitySeq`**, **`readActivitySeq`**, and **`unreadComplete`** to each row for multi-tab UI. |
| POST | **`/coddy/describe`** | JSON **`{"text"}`** to get a short description phrase. |
| POST | **`/coddy/enhance-prompt`** | JSON **`{"text"}`** — rewrites the user's draft into a clearer, more specific prompt through one direct LLM completion without tools. The draft is source text only: it is never answered or executed. Optional **`X-Coddy-Session-ID`** selects that session's effective model; otherwise the endpoint falls back to **`agent.model`**, then the first configured **`models[]`** row. JSON **`{"object":"coddy.enhance_prompt","text"}`**; **`400`** for a blank draft, **`502`** for an LLM failure, and **`503`** when no model is available. The composer replaces the draft with the result and **Ctrl+Z**/**⌘Z** restores the original. |
| GET | **`/coddy/slash-commands`** | Paginated slash commands derived from configured skills (**`page`**, **`page_size`** required). Optional **`prefix`** filters by **`name`** (case-insensitive). Optional **`X-Coddy-Session-ID`** resolves **`${CWD}`** expansion for **`skills.dirs`** like other session-scoped lookups. JSON **`items[].name`** and **`items[].description`**, **`total`**, **`has_more`**. Built-in commands (**`/compact`**, **`/export`**, **`/plugin`**) are not listed here; they are served separately by **`/coddy/commands`**, advertised to editors via the ACP available-commands update, and run deterministically when sent as a prompt (e.g. **`POST /v1/responses`** with **`input:"/plugin marketplace list"`**). |
| GET | **`/coddy/commands`** | Lists the deterministic built-in slash commands (**`/compact`**, **`/export`**, **`/plugin`**) that run without an LLM turn, so the composer can render a **Commands** group beside skills. Optional **`prefix`** filters by **`name`** (case-insensitive). JSON **`{"object":"coddy.commands","items":[{"name","description"}]}`**. **`compact`** is included only while **`compaction.enable`** is true; **`export`** and **`plugin`** are always present. **`/export`** sent as a prompt writes the session transcript to a file in the session workspace (see **`docs/features/session-export.md`**). |
| GET | **`/coddy/skills`** | Lists all skills found in configured **`skills.dirs`**. Optional **`X-Coddy-Session-ID`** resolves **`${CWD}`** in **`skills.dirs`** against that session's workspace, like **`/coddy/slash-commands`** (server default cwd without the header; **`400`** for a malformed id, **`404`** for an unknown session). JSON **`{"object":"coddy.skills_list","items":[...]}`**; each item has **`name`**, **`description`**, **`file_path`**, **`enabled`**, **`version`** (installed version — the marketplace-declared version for synced skills, else the **`SKILL.md`** frontmatter version; absent when unknown), **`source`** (the configured **`skills.sources`** entry when the skill was installed remotely; absent for local/bundled skills), and **`readonly`** (**`true`** for bundled skills, which cannot be deleted). Uses same directory scan and last-wins deduplication as the agent loader. |
| POST | **`/coddy/skills/{name}/enable`** | Removes **`{name}`** from the disabled list in **`ManagedDir`** (`~/.coddy/skills/.disabled`). **`200`** **`{"ok":true}`**; **`400`** when **`name`** contains path separators or is blank. Invalidates the slash-command cache so the next **`/coddy/slash-commands`** call reflects the change. |
| POST | **`/coddy/skills/{name}/disable`** | Adds **`{name}`** to the disabled list. Same response codes and cache invalidation as **`enable`**. |
| POST | **`/coddy/skills/sync`** | Fetches configured skill sources and materializes skills into **`ManagedDir`**. Without **`source`**, syncs every entry in **`skills.sources`**; with **`?source=<src>`**, syncs only that marketplace (a GitHub repo, git URL, or **`marketplace.json`** URL, whether or not it is in the config). Manual only. **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"added":[...],"updated":[...],"failed":[{"source","error"}]}`**. Invalidates the slash-command cache. |
| GET | **`/coddy/skills/updates`** | For every installed remote skill, fetches its marketplace source and compares the installed version against the latest declared upstream (network / git access). **`200`** **`{"object":"coddy.skills_updates","items":[{"name","source","version","latest","update_available"}]}`**. |
| GET | **`/coddy/skills/available`** | Fetches every configured marketplace manifest (network / git) and lists the plugins they advertise for install. **`200`** **`{"object":"coddy.skills_available","items":[{"name","description","version","source","installed"}]}`**. |
| POST | **`/coddy/skills/install`** | JSON **`{"source","plugin"}`**: installs a single named plugin from a marketplace source (not the whole source). **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"added":[...],"updated":[...],"failed":[...]}`**; **`400`** when the plugin or source is unknown. Invalidates the slash-command cache. |
| POST | **`/coddy/skills/{name}/update`** | Re-syncs the marketplace source that provides **`{name}`**, installing the version it currently declares. **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"added":[...],"updated":[...],"failed":[...]}`**; **`400`** when **`{name}`** was not installed from a remote source. Invalidates the slash-command cache. |
| GET | **`/coddy/skills/sources`** | Lists the configured **`skills.sources`** entries. **`200`** **`{"object":"coddy.skills_sources","items":["owner/repo", ...]}`**. |
| POST | **`/coddy/skills/sources`** | JSON **`{"source","sync"}`**: appends **`source`** to **`skills.sources`** in **config.yaml** and reloads config. When **`sync:true`**, also fetches it immediately. **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"added":bool,"sync":{...}}`**; **`400`** on an unrecognized source. |
| DELETE | **`/coddy/skills/sources?source=<src>`** | Removes **`source`** (matched case-insensitively) from **`skills.sources`** in **config.yaml** and reloads config. Installed skills remain. **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"removed":bool}`**; **`400`** when the **`source`** query parameter is missing. |
| DELETE | **`/coddy/skills/{name}`** | Deletes any on-disk skill by name (its directory, plus its remote provenance entry when synced). Bundled (read-only) skills, and skills outside the configured skill directories, return **`400`**. **`200`** **`{"ok":true}`**. Invalidates the slash-command cache. |
| GET | **`/coddy/mcp`** | Merged MCP server list from three levels: **`mcp_servers`** in **config.yaml** and the user-global **`<home>/mcp.json`** (both scope **`global`**), plus the project-local **`.coddy/mcp.json`** (scope **`local`**); mcp.json files are Cursor-compatible and later levels override earlier ones by name. JSON **`{"object":"coddy.mcp_list","workspace":"...","project_trust":"ask","items":[...]}`**; each item has **`name`**, **`source`** (**`global`** / **`local`**), **`origin`** (**`config`** / **`home`** / **`project`** — the owning file), **`readonly`** (**`true`** for config.yaml entries), **`transport`**, **`command`**, **`args`**, **`url`**, **`env`**, **`headers`**, **`source_path`**, **`enabled`**, **`status`** (**`connected`** / **`error`** / **`disabled`** / **`unsupported`** / **`needs_approval`** / **`denied`**), **`error`**, **`trusted`**, **`gated`**, **`fingerprint`**, **`tools`** (**`[{name, description, enabled}]`**), **`disabled_tools`**. Enabled servers are probed for tools over their transport (**`stdio`** spawn, **`http`** streamable with legacy-SSE fallback, **`sse`**; connect, **`tools/list`**, close) with results cached until the definition changes; **`?refresh=1`** re-probes. Unknown transport types report **`unsupported`** without probing. A project-local entry that the workspace trust gate holds back is **never probed**: it reports **`needs_approval`** (or **`denied`**) with **`trusted:false`**, no tools, and the declaration an approval would cover. |
| POST | **`/coddy/mcp/{name}/enable`** | Clears the server's disabled flag, persisting into the file that defines it (**config.yaml** **`disabled`** or **`disabled`** in the owning mcp.json), then reloads config. **`200`** **`{"ok":true}`**; **`400`** for an unknown server. Live sessions pick the change up on their next turn. |
| POST | **`/coddy/mcp/{name}/disable`** | Sets the server's disabled flag in the owning file. Same responses as **`enable`**. New sessions skip connecting the server; live sessions stop seeing its tools on the next turn. |
| POST | **`/coddy/mcp/{name}/tools/{tool}/enable`** | Removes **`{tool}`** from the server's disabled-tools list (**`disabled_tools`** in YAML, **`disabledTools`** in the owning mcp.json). **`200`** **`{"ok":true}`**; **`400`** for an unknown server. |
| POST | **`/coddy/mcp/{name}/tools/{tool}/disable`** | Adds **`{tool}`** to the server's disabled-tools list. The tool is hidden from the agent's tool list and rejected at dispatch. Same responses as the tool **`enable`**. |
| POST | **`/coddy/mcp/{name}/trust`** | Approves the **current** declaration of a project-local server for the server's workspace, so sessions may start it. The approval is bound to the workspace and to a digest of the command-bearing declaration (transport, command, args, env, url, headers) and is recorded in **`<home>/mcp-trust.json`** with a receipt (env and header **names** only). **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"fingerprint":"sha256:…"}`**; **`400`** for an unknown server, for a **config.yaml** / **`<home>/mcp.json`** entry (those need no approval), or under **`mcp.project_trust: deny`**. Rewriting the entry withdraws the approval. |
| POST | **`/coddy/mcp/{name}/untrust`** | Withdraws the workspace approval. **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"removed":<bool>}`**. Sessions already holding a connected client keep it; new sessions no longer start the server. |
| POST | **`/coddy/mcp/project-trust`** | Sets **`mcp.project_trust`** in **config.yaml** and reloads it. Body **`{"policy":"ask"\|"allow"\|"deny"}`**. **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"project_trust":"…"}`**; **`400`** for an unknown value. The bundled UI edits this in the MCP servers tab, next to the servers it governs. |
| GET | **`/coddy/subagents`** | Subagent definitions visible from a workspace (**`?cwd=<absolute path>`**, default: the server's default cwd; a relative path is **`400`**): the embedded built-ins (**`general`**, **`explore`**), user-scope files under **`${CODDY_HOME}/agents`**, and project-scope files under the workspace's **`.claude/agents`** and **`.coddy/agents`** (**`subagents.dirs`**, later directories win by name). **`{"object":"coddy.subagent_list","workspace","policy","items":[...]}`** where **`workspace`** is the canonical path receipts are keyed by, **`policy`** the effective **`subagents.project_trust`**, and each item carries **`name`**, **`description`**, **`scope`** (**`builtin`**, **`user`**, **`project`**), **`path`**, **`digest`** (SHA-256 of the definition bytes, the embedded bytes for built-ins), **`model`**, **`mode`**, **`builtin`**, **`hidden`**, and the trust decision for that workspace: **`trust`** (**`trusted`** or **`needs_approval`**) mirrored as the booleans **`trusted`** and **`needs_approval`**. Under **`deny`** project directories are not read at all. See **`docs/features/subagents.md`**. |
| POST | **`/coddy/subagents/{name}/trust`** | Approves the **current** content of a project-scope definition for a workspace: records a receipt in **`<home>/subagents-trust.json`** bound to the canonical workspace, the name and the file digest, so **`spawn_agent`** may run it under **`project_trust: ask`**. Rewriting the file withdraws the approval. Optional body **`{"cwd": ...}`** (default: the server's default cwd); **`cwd`** must be the session's **server-side** workspace, the `cwd` field of the **`GET /coddy/sessions`** rows or **`GET /coddy/workspace/context`** with the session header, since receipts are keyed by that path. This route is the approval path for a remote console or ACP client, whose local `coddy agents trust` writes a receipt on the wrong machine. **`200`** **`{"object":"coddy.subagent","item":<catalog entry>}`** with the refreshed entry; **`404`** when no definition of that name is visible from the workspace; **`400`** for a built-in or user-scope definition (nothing to approve), a malformed body, or a relative **`cwd`**. |
| POST | **`/coddy/subagents/{name}/untrust`** | Withdraws the receipt of a definition for a workspace (same optional body). Withdrawing an approval that was never on file changes nothing. **`200`** with the refreshed entry; **`404`** unknown name; **`400`** malformed body or relative **`cwd`**. |
| GET | **`/coddy/hooks`** | Hook definition files a session with this workspace would load (**`?cwd=<absolute path>`**, default: the server's default cwd; a relative path is **`400`**), in load order (**`hooks.files`**: the operator's **`${CODDY_HOME}/hooks.json`**, then the workspace's **`.claude/settings.json`**, **`.claude/settings.local.json`** and **`.coddy/hooks.json`**). **`{"object":"coddy.hook_list","workspace","policy","items":[...]}`** where **`workspace`** is the canonical path receipts are keyed by, **`policy`** the effective **`hooks.project_trust`**, and each item carries **`file`** (the name receipts and the CLI use: the workspace-relative path for project scope, the absolute path otherwise), **`path`**, **`scope`** (**`user`**, **`project`**), **`digest`** (SHA-256 of the file), the trust decision for that workspace (**`trust`**, mirrored as **`trusted`** and **`needs_approval`**), **`error`** for a file that does not parse, **`warnings`**, and **`hooks`**: one row per handler (**`event`**, **`matcher`**, **`type`**, **`command`**, **`args`**, **`timeout_seconds`**, **`async`**, **`fail_closed`**, **`unsupported`**). Under **`deny`** project files are not read at all. See **`docs/features/hooks.md`**. |
| POST | **`/coddy/hooks/trust`** | Approves the **current** content of a project-scope hooks file for a workspace: records a receipt in **`<home>/hooks-trust.json`** bound to the canonical workspace, the file and its digest, so its hooks run under **`hooks.project_trust: ask`** from the next turn. Rewriting the file withdraws the approval. Body **`{"cwd": ..., "file": ...}`**: **`cwd`** must be the session's **server-side** workspace (default: the server's default cwd), **`file`** the name **`GET /coddy/hooks`** lists. This route is the approval path for a remote console or ACP client, whose local `coddy hooks trust` writes a receipt on the wrong machine. **`200`** **`{"object":"coddy.hook_source","item":<catalog entry>}`** with the refreshed entry; **`404`** when no such file is visible from the workspace; **`400`** for a user-scope file (nothing to approve), a file that does not parse, a missing **`file`**, a malformed body, or a relative **`cwd`**. |
| POST | **`/coddy/hooks/untrust`** | Withdraws the receipt of a file for a workspace (same body). Withdrawing an approval that was never on file changes nothing. **`200`** with the refreshed entry; **`404`** unknown file; **`400`** missing **`file`**, malformed body or relative **`cwd`**. |
| PUT | **`/coddy/mcp/{name}`** | Upserts one named entry in an mcp.json file. **`?scope=local`** (default) targets the project **`.coddy/mcp.json`** under the server's default cwd; **`?scope=global`** targets the user-global **`<home>/mcp.json`**. JSON body is the Cursor-format entry: **`command`**, **`args`**, **`env`** (object), **`url`**, **`headers`** (object), **`disabled`**, **`disabledTools`**. Requires **`command`** or **`url`**; **`400`** when the name contains **`__`**, spaces, or path separators, the scope is unknown, or the body is invalid. **`200`** **`{"ok":true}`**. Config.yaml-defined servers are edited via **`PUT /coddy/config`** instead. |
| DELETE | **`/coddy/mcp/{name}`** | Removes the named entry from the mcp.json file that defines it (project or global). **`400`** for config.yaml-defined or unknown servers. **`200`** **`{"ok":true}`**. |
| GET | **`/coddy/workspace/files`** | Paginated workspace listing under session **cwd** (**`page`**, **`page_size`** required). Non-blank **case-insensitive** substring **`prefix`** on **`path_rel`**; omit or blank **`prefix`** yields empty **`items`**. **`dirs=true`** adds directory rows (**`kind`** **`dir`**, **`path_rel`** trailing **`/`**). JSON **`items[].name`**, **`items[].path_rel`**, **`items[].kind`** (**`file`** or **`dir`**), **`total`**, **`has_more`**. |
| GET | **`/coddy/workspace/file`** | One workspace text file as display lines, for the composer's line-range picker. Required **`path_rel`** (workspace-relative, never escapes session **cwd**); optional **`max_lines`** (1 to 5000, default 2000). JSON **`path_rel`**, **`mime_type`**, **`lines[]`** (no terminators; a trailing newline adds no empty last line and CRLF loses the trailing carriage return), **`total_lines`** (whole file), **`truncated`**. Legacy encodings decode to UTF-8; files over 512 KiB are refused. **`400`** for a directory, undecodable content, a traversing path or a bad **`max_lines`**; **`404`** for a missing file. |
| GET | **`/coddy/workspace/context`** | Workspace context for the composer chips: **`path`**, **`name`**, **`is_git_repo`**, **`is_worktree`**, plus **`repo_root`**, **`branch`**, **`branches`**, **`worktrees[]`** (**`path`**, **`branch`**, **`main`**) inside a git repository. Uses the session **cwd** from **`X-Coddy-Session-ID`** (server default cwd without the header). Optional **`path`** query describes an explicit folder instead (pre-session preview); a missing folder yields **`400`**. Git data degrades gracefully when the **`git`** binary is absent (**`is_git_repo:false`**). |
| GET | **`/coddy/workspace/folders`** | Direct subfolders of **`path`** (default: session **cwd**) for the workspace folder picker: **`{"path","parent","folders":[{"name","path"}]}`**. Hidden folders and **`node_modules`** are skipped; rows sorted by name. Missing folder yields **`400`**. **`path=:drives:`** returns the machine's drive roots instead (**`{"drives":true,"folders":[{"name":"C:","path":"C:\\"}]}`**, **`path`** = **`parent`** = **`:drives:`**); on a host with no drive letters (Linux, macOS) the sentinel is just an unknown folder (**`400`**). A drive root reports **`"parent":":drives:"`**, which is how the picker walks up out of a volume — everywhere else **`parent`** stays the real parent directory. |
| POST | **`/coddy/workspace/folders`** | Creates one subfolder for the folder picker: **`{"path","name"}`** makes **`name`** inside **`path`** (default: session **cwd**) and answers with the **listing of the new folder** (**`{"path","parent","folders":[]}`**), so the picker steps into it and **Open** picks it. **`name`** is a single entry: empty, **`.`**, **`..`**, a volume name, or anything containing **`/`** or **`\`** yields **`400`**. A parent that does not exist yields **`400`** and the chain is never created; **`path=:drives:`** yields **`400`** because the volume level has no directory behind it. A name already taken yields **`409`**. |
| GET | **`/coddy/config/schema`** | JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for the settings editor. Describes the same logical fields as **`ConfigJSON`** with **`description`**, **`default`**, **`pattern`** on **`providers[].name`**, optional **`x-coddy-*`** hints (for example **`x-coddy-provider-api-key-env-placeholder`** on **`providers[].api_key`** for dynamic placeholders), and **`x-coddy-property-order`** for section order. **`httpserver`** is omitted (listen bind stays on the **`coddy serve`** CLI). **`GET`** / **`PUT`** **`/coddy/config`** still return the full document including **`httpserver`** when present in YAML. |
| GET | **`/coddy/config/reasoning-levels`** | Reasoning levels the **`?model=`** logical id offers when **`models[].reasoning_levels`** is not overridden, for the settings form's **Fetch reasoning levels** button. Detection is model-id based (**`gpt-5*`** and **`gpt-6*`** -> **`minimal,low,medium,high`**; OpenAI **`o`**-series, **`gpt-oss*`**, **`qwen3*`**, Claude extended-thinking -> **`low,medium,high`**). The provider type decides the Codex remap (**`minimal`** becomes **`none`**): optional **`?provider_type=`** carries the type of the provider row as it stands in the (unsaved) form and wins over the saved config, so a provider that is not saved yet, or whose type was just changed, resolves the way it will after Save; without it the provider prefix is looked up in the active config, and an unknown prefix gets the un-remapped list. The id need not exist in **`models[]`**, and a saved override is ignored - the button reports what the id offers, not what is configured. **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"model":...,"levels":[...],"detected":true}`**; a model with no reasoning support is **`{"ok":true,"levels":[],"detected":false}`**, not an error; a malformed id is **`200`** with **`{"ok":false,"error":...}`** so the form can show it inline; a missing **`model`** parameter is **`400`** with the same flat **`{"ok":false,"error":...}`** body the other **`/coddy/config`** routes use. |
| GET | **`/coddy/config`** | Current process configuration as JSON (same logical fields as **`config.yaml`**, including secrets). Per-session path fields (**`skills.dirs`**, **`subagents.dirs`**, **`hooks.files`**, **`prompts.dir`**, **`mcp_servers[].command`** / **`args`** / **`url`** / **`env`** / **`headers`**) are returned as written in the file, including a **`${CWD}`** placeholder; **`${CODDY_HOME}`** and the process-scoped directories are returned expanded. |
| POST | **`/coddy/config/validate`** | Body is **`ConfigJSON`**. **`200`** with **`{"ok":true}`** when valid, **`400`** with **`{"ok":false,"error":"..."}`** otherwise. |
| PUT | **`/coddy/config`** | Body is **`ConfigJSON`**. Validates, writes **`config.yaml`** atomically, reloads in-process config for HTTP handlers and new agent turns. The file is rewritten **over its current content**: comments (including commented-out keys) and the existing key order survive the save, and a file that carries no **`# yaml-language-server: $schema=`** header gets the published one (**`https://coddy.dev/config.schema.json`**) so editors keep validating it; a header pointing somewhere else is left as it is. Changed **`mcp_servers`** are reconnected for active sessions, re-running the workspace trust gate so an unapproved project declaration is not started; a session with a turn in flight is reconnected when that turn ends, not mid-turn; ACP client-provided per-session servers remain connected. **`200`** **`{"ok":true}`**; **`400`** on validation failure; **`500`** if the file was written but reload failed (server restores **`config.yaml.bak`** over the primary path when possible). |

| GET | **`/coddy/providers/{name}/neuraldeep-auth`** | Non-secret NeuralDeep sign-in status: **`connected`**, display **`masked`** key, optional **`key_name`**, and **`source`** - the credential requests actually use (`oauth`, `api_key`, `api_key_command`, `env`, or `none`; an explicit key wins over a stored login). **`hub`** names the hub that issued the stored login and **`endpoint_hub`** the hub a sign-in for the endpoint in the optional **`?api_base=`** query (default: the saved row's, falling back to the default deployment) would use; Settings passes the endpoint picked in the form and warns when the two differ, since a key minted by one deployment is not honored by the other. | GET | **`/coddy/providers/{name}/usage`** | Account usage behind a provider row, for the status bar of every surface (design record **`docs/plans/neuraldeep-usage.md`**). Today only **`type: neuraldeep`** has a source (the hub's read-only **`GET /v1/limits`**, read with the row's own credential and **`proxy`**). **`200`** **`{"ok":true,"usage":{...}}`** with the **`provider_usage`** update: **`plan`**, **`keyName`**, **`windows[]`** (**`id`** `session`/`week`/`day`, **`label`**, optional **`used`**/**`limit`**/**`remaining`**, **`usedPercent`**, **`exhausted`**, **`resetsAt`** on the hub's clock, **`resetInSec`** age-corrected), **`rate`** (the live minute), **`cooldownSec`**, **`wallet`** (**`balanceRub`**, **`spentRub30d`**, the account's own rubles, possibly negative), **`blocked`** with **`blockers`** and **`retryAt`**/**`retryInSec`**, **`unlimited`** and **`unlimitedModels`** (upstream ids that bypass the windows), **`blockedModels`** (upstream ids the key may not call now, each with **`blocker`**, **`retryAt`** and **`retryInSec`** - a gate over part of the catalogue, so **`blocked`** stays false and only these models are refused), **`observedAt`**, **`fetchedAt`**, **`refreshPending`**/**`refreshInSec`** when the hub's pacing deferred a refresh, **`resuming`** only on the frames the agent itself sends on the turn stream while a turn waits for a hit limit to lift (**`agent.wait_for_limit_reset`**; a rejected key, `unauthorized`, comes without them, and a non-kind failure adds **`detail`**); **`404`** unknown provider. **`?refresh=1`** asks for a fresh read: the manager serves its cache for 20 s, refreshes at once when the last read is 15 s or older, and otherwise defers the read to the end of that floor (the answer says so). | GET | **`/coddy/sessions/{id}/composer-stream`** | **`text/event-stream`** relay of the live **agent**/**plan**/**ask** turn (same SSE as **`POST /v1/responses`** with **`stream: true`**).
